\hlchaptermodality{303}

\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can order the steps of a story: at first, first of all, then, at the very end and ultimately.}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{ابتدا} (ebtedâ)}{ابتدا (ebtedâ)}]{\fa{ابتدا} (ebtedâ) — at first, at the start}

\label{lesson:FA-C303-ebteda}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to come to an end, then the Persian for finally.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{ابتدا}}
\textbf{\fa{ابتدا}} (\emph{ebtedâ}) — \textquotedblleft{}at first, at the start\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{ابتدا} \fa{همه} \fa{ساکت} \fa{بودند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Ebtedâ hame sâket budand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
At first everyone was quiet.
\end{quote}

Formal; in speech \emph{avval}. Also a noun: \emph{dar ebtedâ-ye râh} \textquotedblleft{}at the start of the road\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ebtedâ} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{ibtidā'}, \textquotedblleft{}a beginning\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB lists the Arabic source).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ebtedâ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ebtedâ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{ebtedâ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to come to an end, then the Persian for finally, then say \emph{ebtedâ} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{نخست} (nakhost)}{نخست (nakhost)}]{\fa{نخست} (nakhost) — first, firstly}

\label{lesson:FA-C303-nakhost}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for finally, then the Persian for at first.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{نخست}}
\textbf{\fa{نخست}} (\emph{nakhost}) — \textquotedblleft{}first, firstly\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{نخست} \fa{نامه} \fa{را} \fa{خواند} \fa{و} \fa{بعد} \fa{گریه} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Nakhost nâme râ khând va ba'd gerye kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
First she read the letter, and then she cried.
\end{quote}

Literary; \emph{nakhost vazir} \textquotedblleft{}prime minister\textquotedblright{}. In speech \emph{avval}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{nakhost} is inherited from Middle Persian \emph{naxust}, \textquotedblleft{}first\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nakhost}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{nakhost}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for finally, then the Persian for at first, then say \emph{nakhost} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{آنگاه} (ângâh)}{آنگاه (ângâh)}]{\fa{آنگاه} (ângâh) — then, at that point}

\label{lesson:FA-C303-angah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for at first, then the Persian for first.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{آنگاه}}
\textbf{\fa{آنگاه}} (\emph{ângâh}) — \textquotedblleft{}then, at that point\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{شام} \fa{خوردیم} \fa{و} \fa{آنگاه} \fa{به} \fa{پارک} \fa{رفتیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Shâm khordim va ângâh be pârk raftim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We had dinner and then went to the park.
\end{quote}

Literary; in speech \emph{ba'd}. In writing it can answer an \emph{agar} clause: \textquotedblleft{}if ..., then ...\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ângâh} is built from Persian \emph{ân} \textquotedblleft{}that\textquotedblright{} and \emph{gâh} \textquotedblleft{}time, place\textquotedblright{}, both native words: \textquotedblleft{}that time\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ângâh}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ângâh}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{ângâh}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for at first, then the Persian for first, then say \emph{ângâh} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{دست} \fa{آخر} (dast-e âkhar)}{دست آخر (dast-e âkhar)}]{\fa{دست} \fa{آخر} (dast-e âkhar) — at the very end, in the end (colloquial)}

\label{lesson:FA-C303-dast-e-akhar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for first, then the Persian for then.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{دست} \fa{آخر}}
\textbf{\fa{دست} \fa{آخر}} (\emph{dast-e âkhar}) — \textquotedblleft{}at the very end, in the end (colloquial)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{دست} \fa{آخر} \fa{همه} \fa{با} \fa{هم} \fa{شام} \fa{خوردیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dast-e âkhar hame bâ ham shâm khordim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the end we all had dinner together.
\end{quote}

Conversational. Literally \textquotedblleft{}the last hand\textquotedblright{}, as in a card game. Written without the ezafe sign, read \emph{dast-e}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{dast} \textquotedblleft{}hand\textquotedblright{} is inherited, from Old Persian \emph{dasta-} (EtymDB); \emph{âkhar} \textquotedblleft{}last\textquotedblright{} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{ākhir} (EtymDB). The phrase is the last hand of a game.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dast-e âkhar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dast-e âkhar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{dast-e âkhar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for first, then the Persian for then, then say \emph{dast-e âkhar} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{در} \fa{نهایت} (dar nahâyat)}{در نهایت (dar nahâyat)}]{\fa{در} \fa{نهایت} (dar nahâyat) — ultimately, in the end}

\label{lesson:FA-C303-dar-nahayat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for then, then the Persian for at the very end.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{در} \fa{نهایت}}
\textbf{\fa{در} \fa{نهایت}} (\emph{dar nahâyat}) — \textquotedblleft{}ultimately, in the end\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{نهایت} \fa{تصمیم} \fa{گرفتیم} \fa{در} \fa{خانه} \fa{بمانیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dar nahâyat tasmim gereftim dar khâne bemânim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Ultimately we decided to stay at home.
\end{quote}

\emph{nahâyat} alone means \textquotedblleft{}the utmost\textquotedblright{}: \emph{nahâyat-e lotf} \textquotedblleft{}the height of kindness\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{nahâyat} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{nihāya}, \textquotedblleft{}end, limit\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB lists the Arabic source); \emph{dar} \textquotedblleft{}in\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dar nahâyat}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for then, then the Persian for at the very end, then say \emph{dar nahâyat} again
\end{itemize}
